chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Zakariya al-Mawsili (known as Kokab al-Dam), who said: I heard the Servant of God (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever performs Hajj forty times, it will be said to him: 'Intercede for whomever you wish,' and a gate of Paradise will be opened for him, through which he and those for whom he intercedes will enter.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Hajj forty times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from the Imams to emphasize the cumulative spiritual merit of longevity and consistent devotion, specifically linking a lifespan of forty years or more to the reward of forty Hajj pilgrimages. The promise of interceding for any chosen individual underscores the Imamate’s authority in granting salvation, while the opening of a specific gate of Paradise illustrates the tangible, hierarchical rewards of the Hereafter in Shia eschatology.
